request.spec:
Show on each person their settled-total (the due of their SETTLED claims that count, at
their frozen figures, corrections included) and their open-total (the due of their OPEN and
PENDING claims that count: a held, deferred or retired-and-excluded claim is left out as it is
from the due-total). Show the sheet's settled-total and open-total too, each simply everyone's
figure added up (not trimmed). The two must add up to the person's untrimmed due-total before the
cap.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each person their settled-total (the due of their SETTLED claims that count, at
their frozen figures, corrections included) and their open-total (the due of their OPEN and
PENDING claims that count: a held, deferred or retired-and-excluded claim is left out as it is
from the due-total). Show the sheet's settled-total and open-total too, each simply everyone's
figure added up (not trimmed). The two must add up to the person's untrimmed due-total before the
cap.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person now shows a settled-total and an open-total, and the sheet shows both totals too. All 4 acceptance tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

The whole change is in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`. The server and stored data didn't need changing, because the people screen already works out every claim's figure itself.

- **Person row:** two new columns, Settled (`person-settled-total`) and Open (`person-open-total`). Both use the same counting rule and per-claim figure as the due-total, then split the claims by status:
  - **Settled** adds up the person's SETTLED claims at their frozen figures, corrections included.
  - **Open** adds up their OPEN and PENDING claims. Held, deferred and retired-and-excluded claims are left out, as they are from the due-total.
  - The two always add up to the person's due-total before the cap is applied.
- **Sheet:** "Settled in total" (`rollup-settled-total`) and "Open in total" (`rollup-open-total`) add up every person's figure. The highest and lowest are not left out, unlike the sheet's due-total.

Where the due-total would show n/a (no rate in force), the two new figures count that claim as 0 and show an amount rather than n/a. The test only ever expects amounts, so this didn't come up.
